input:
City of Northvale — Online Permits (discovery call transcript, cleaned up)

Director: Residents and contractors apply for building permits online instead of in person. Phase 1 is residential building permits only; event and parking permits are phase 2, not now.
Permit officer: An application needs site address (validated against the city's address register), owner details, contractor licence number, drawings as PDF, and the fee. Fees depend on project value — we use a fee table that changes every April.
Director: Applicants pay by card online. Fee waivers exist for registered charities; an officer must approve each waiver.
Permit officer: We review in this order: completeness check (2 days), plan review (up to 15 days), then inspection scheduling. If something's missing, we send it back and the clock stops.
IT: Must use the city's existing single sign-on for staff. Residents sign in with email. Everything must be in English and Spanish. We have to keep applications for 7 years.
Director: Applicants should always know where their application is and what's holding it up. Our goal is to cut average approval time from 45 days to 20.
Permit officer: Inspectors book inspections in the field on tablets, record pass/fail with notes and photos.
Comms: Public dashboard showing number of permits issued per month by neighbourhood.
